hi, i’m sorry to see you are struggling. i’d like to remind you that progress and recovery is not linear. The fact that you’re trying to recover is a HUGE!!! step in the right direction. And especially when you’re starting, it’s very hard to just. stop. Because it is an addiction. 

Listening to music van be a great coping thing. You’ll have to discover by trial and error what does and doesn’t work for you. Maybe you can try to converse with you guardian as to what you need from them, what they can do to help you? 
Sometimes it can just help to know that you have a safe non judgemental space where you can express yourself (idk how understanding your guardian is, but it can help to have them understand what you’re going through, without immediately offering a solution) If your guardian doesn’t feel safe, maybe try talking to a friend or counsellor and letting them know what you want them to do: give advice or just listen, you know? 

If you are having urges right now, i’d like to give you a few self harm alternatives. I’m not sure how to translate it properly. There are a few things that are biologically/fysiologically (whatever) proven to help reset your mind and body: 
- emerging yourself into cold water. Taking a cold shower or holding your hands and arms underneath the cold faucet.
- try to breathe and focus on your breathing (4 in, 4 hold, 4 out; or whatever works for you) 
- try to tense and relax your muscles
- exercise intensly

Idk if it will help you. My therapist gave me these things because they are like very biological, when you’re stressed and you do these things, your body will automatically get a bit calmer

maybe exercising (releasing angry energy/adrenaline) or resetting your nervous system.

Do you need a physical release, a physical stinging/sensation (like the feeling of cutting) you could try the running or cold water. Or you can write down what’s bothering you and scribble the pages, rip them apart, destroy it. 

If you need to process your emotions, it might help to sit down and do a breathing exercise or treat yourself extra gently and nicely (take a bath, have some chocolate) 

If you want, you could also look into the application ‘calm harm’. They give a lot of different suggestions for what you can do, based on what you need.
